fun_highlights: The callback system is the best thing in the game. When Calla (D4) strays at 44 and the same decision comes back at 67 — 'Confess it to someone' / 'Take it with you' — the choice actually MEANS something because the previous act is on record. Similarly, when Anders Aldecott (D13) at age 55 goes back to the town he left at age 42, the exact age he left is echoed in the prose. This is choice-with-memory, and it lands.

The vocation fork genuinely differentiates adult lives at a structural level. A soldier's life (D7 Caleb's war-era path: combat assignment at 22, war loss at 47, a ghost at the end) reads nothing like a scholar's (D2 Henrik: lean study bet, knowledge-guard at 68, scholar's peace at 73). The five-way calling choice at youth — and the distinct adult card cluster it unlocks — delivers real divergence across the content.js vocation arcs.

The 'competing goods' cards (x_honest_or_kind, x_loyalty_truth, x_dream_or_duty) have genuinely no clean answer. D4's Noor at 59 choosing to tell a truth that costs a friendship is a real dilemma with real shape — the hint text 'honesty' vs 'loyalty' refuses to editorialize. These are the game's best choices because both roads are defensible.

The era system creates genuine tonal variety at the dynasty level. D6 (plague era) Tomas choosing to tend the dying at 59 lands differently than D7 (war era) Caleb's choice about whether to serve or dodge. The world-condition shapes what the moral pressure IS, not just what the prose says.

The bequest mechanic (e_bequest) is a real lever: choosing 'nothing but their own freedom' or 'the stories and warmth' visibly changes what the heir screen says and seeds different start conditions. It makes the final choice of a life feel consequential across the generation boundary — something to plan toward.

The 'guarded' and 'bookish' trait-gated moments (t_guarded, t_bookish) are the clearest examples of choices that characterfully reflect who this person already IS. 'Let them in. Just this once.' vs 'Keep the wall.' plays completely differently when the character has carried that wall for decades. This is the game honoring its own characterization.
staleness: The calling choice at youth fires in every single life via near-certainty forcing (engine.js: 'near-certain once past the window's midpoint'), and the four options are worded identically every time. In the 15 dynasties, every adult life that reaches youth presents the exact same four-way fork with the same button text: 'The blade — a soldier's life.', 'The book — the scholar's road.', 'The hands — a maker's trade.', 'The road — go where the work is.' The scene prose varies slightly by era/standing, but the options themselves never change across all 15 dynasties. It becomes the one predictable beat a player learns to expect.

The body-deterioration observation pool is enormous in content.js (18 lines for vit_tire, 16 for vit_neg) but the per-life cap of 4 ambient observations means the same 2-3 body lines appear in nearly every late-life transcript. D4's Hale at 53: 'The weather has begun living in his joints.' D6's Cassian at 57: 'Mornings take longer to arrive.' D13's Anders at 74: 'He has noticed the handrail.' The cap stops flood but the lines still cluster because high-vit late lives reliably hit 1-2 of these regardless of what else is happening.

The marriage beat (a_marry) shows 8 different scene framings — era-colored, vocation-colored, a deep general pool — but the choice is always binary: 'Ask. Build a life.' / 'Not yet. Maybe never.' Across 15 dynasties this exact binary appears at least 20 times. The framing varies; the actual decision never does. A marriage with a specific person in a specific context asks the same abstract question every time, which flattens what should be the most personal beat in a life.

Three epitaphs recur verbatim in the 15-dynasty run. D5's Ottilie: 'Lived half in the world and half in her own head.' D15's Saoirse Brandt: 'Lived half in the world and half in her own head.' D13's Anders Lindqvist (5th of line): 'Kept a whole country behind the eyes, and lived there often.' D9's Cassian Thorne: 'Kept a whole country behind the eyes, and lived there often.' Dynasty.js has a 150-line session-global blocker (RECENT_LINES) but the pool per cluster is only 3-4 entries for mind/spirit themes, so 15 dynasties outruns it. The epitaph is the game's most visible final flourish — repetition here is the worst place for it.

The 'began from nothing' card (s_from_nothing) fires in D1's Saoirse at 33, D3's Cassian at 29, D5's Ottilie at 40, D12's Mira at 45 — four times in the same session. The text is near-identical each time: 'There is nothing behind [name]...' and the choices ('Build, brick by brick.' / 'Find others to climb with.') never vary. The onceDyn cooldown is set to true (3 generations) but multiple dynasties are single-generation, which resets the counter frequently enough to bring this back in nearly every low-standing house.

The reputation choice (a_make_name) fires for Saoirse D1 at 44, Henrik D2 at 38, Noor D4 at 32, Vesna D6 at age ~, multiple others — and every time it uses the same scene: 'is at the age where a reputation sets, the way a face does. There is still a little say in which one.' The three options are identically worded across all instances. For a choice_savorer, a reputation-defining decision that reads exactly the same way regardless of who made it, what they've done, what era they live in, is a missed opportunity: this should be the most personal-feeling choice and it is the most template-feeling.

improvements.what: Give the vocation fork a second choice-option per calling that is vocation-specific — e.g. for soldier, 'The body-tax' vs 'The belonging' as a second question about WHY they chose it, not just THAT they chose it. Or, alternatively, vary the button text by era (a war-era blade-choice should read differently than a peace-era one).
improvements.why: The calling fork is the most-seen choice in the game. Its near-certainty means a player sees it in every life. When the options are invariant across 15 dynasties, it trains players to treat it as a menu, not a dilemma. One characterful variation by era or context would restore the sense that this life's particular version of the choice is its own.

improvements.what: Add 2-3 more marriage scene framings that vary by CHARACTER HISTORY, not just vocation/era. For example: if the player has 'unspoken_love' in memory (let love slip at youth), the marriage scene could acknowledge the second chance explicitly. If they've 'looked_away' twice, the scene could note their pattern of avoidance. The binary choice can stay; the context should not.
improvements.why: Marriage is the most-repeated binary in the transcripts. It never plays differently even when the person's entire life history changes. Framing it through 2-3 memory flags would make the choice feel specific to THIS person's path rather than the universal 'ask or don't' question.

improvements.what: Expand each epitaph cluster from 3-4 lines to 6-8. The mind/spirit clusters ('lived half in the world and half in their own head', 'kept a whole country behind the eyes') are the shortest pools and also the most common clusters for long-lived intellectual characters. 15 dynasties has already exhausted them.
improvements.why: The epitaph is the final sentence of a life — the one line a player will remember most. It is also, currently, the staleness point with the highest visibility. A doubled pool costs nothing and the dynasty.js anti-repeat machinery will work better when it has more options to work with.

improvements.what: Make the a_make_name reputation-setting card reflect who the person has BEEN so far. If they have 'took_a_stand' in memory, the scholarly option should reference standing against something. If they have 'soldier_blooded', the 'hard to cross' option should acknowledge the blade. The three choices can stay — the scene text and the option hints should feel earned.
improvements.why: For a choice_savorer, a reputation-defining moment that is purely abstract — same words for a war-scarred soldier and a bookish scholar — dissolves the sense that this person is who we think they are. The flag system already tracks what they've been; using it in the scene framing would make this feel like a culmination rather than a menu.

improvements.what: Implement a soft block on the s_from_nothing card when the same dynasty has seen it in the previous 2 lives (use onceDyn:2 instead of once:true, and add an explicit dynasty-level counter). Single-generation dynasties are resetting the cooldown too fast.
improvements.why: This card fires 4+ times in a 15-dynasty session. The problem is structural: every new dynasty resets S.seenDyn, so a run of short single-generation houses brings this exact card and its identical choice back repeatedly. The session-level staleness fix used elsewhere in the epitaph system (RECENT_CLUSTERS) should be extended here.

verdict: A Life has real bones as a choice game: the callback system produces genuine pay-off moments, the vocation arcs differentiate lives at a structural level, and the competing-goods cards are some of the most honest dilemmas in the genre. But a session of 15 dynasties exposes the template underneath: the calling fork looks identical in every life, the marriage binary is invariant across decades and characters, three epitaphs repeat verbatim, and the reputation-setting moment reads the same for a veteran soldier as for a gentle scholar. The pull to play another dynasty is real — the game earns that — but by dynasty 8 or 9 a practiced player is filling in beats before they arrive, and that is the staleness this genre cannot survive.
